flow: file-derived capture dates -> keyword-detected time scope -> scoped evidence search -> negative scope

migration.live_upgrade: the running application database upgraded at container startup; all recordings and indexes unchanged

bulk_file_dates.rule: dates derive from each recording's stored modification time; only recordings without a date are updated; a user-set date is never overwritten

positive_case.query: Did the robot move a cup under the machine today?
positive_case.result: match in one source check of 8 frames at 17.88-20.14 seconds
positive_case.note_shown: Time scope: 2026-11-19 (detected in your question). Recordings without a capture date were skipped.

negative_case.result: no indexed candidates, zero source checks
negative_case.note_shown: No more candidates remain in this search... Time scope: 2026-11-18. Recordings without a capture date were skipped.
negative_case.honesty: the page still states that no match does not prove absence

limits: Capture dates are calendar days, not instants; a recording spanning midnight is counted on its start date only.
File-modification times are an approximation of capture time; users can override any recording's date.
Free-text detection covers only today, yesterday, this/last week and this/last month, and shows the applied scope; explicit selector choices remain authoritative.
Recordings without a capture date are skipped by scoped searches and reported in coverage.
